verdict.rationale: Metronome documents prepaid and postpaid commitments, prepaid credit batches with auto-recharge, and subscription rates on rate cards alongside usage-based billing, which covers credits, commitments and hybrid subscription-plus-usage. The evidence never names tiered, volume, graduated or per-unit pricing models, and the subscription workflows it shows are API-driven rather than clearly no-code. missing for 10: documented tiered/volume/graduated/per-unit pricing models, explicit overage pricing, evidence that a finance lead can configure pricing without code (UI-based rate card setup), independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a finance lead, I can price with tiered, volume, graduated, per-unit, and hybrid subscription-plus-usage models — including credits, commitments, and overage — without custom code

citations.quote: Set up Metronome to support enterprise deal requirements like prepaid and postpaid commitments, negotiated discounts, one-time charges, contract renewals, and more.
Set up Metronome to allow customers to purchase a batch of credits upfront, with auto-recharge or gated access when credits run out.
To change the price of a subscription, change the price of the associated subscription rate on the rate card.
